::: {.tldr}
Every IE study involving human subjects needs IRB approval **at every hub
collecting or analyzing identifiable data**. Most IE studies route through
both Yale's HSC and either IFMR's HSC (for India) or NHRC (for Nepal).
Start the process at least eight weeks before planned launch.
:::

::: {.ie-specific}
J-PAL's [IRB proposals resource]({{< meta var.jpal-research-resources >}})
covers the generic IRB landscape well. This page covers what's specific to IE:
which IRBs we route through, who at each hub coordinates submission, the
templates we use, and how modifications and continuing reviews are handled
when responsibility crosses hubs.
:::

## Which IRB do I need?

Your study's IRB requirements depend on **where data is collected**, **where
it is analyzed**, and **whether subjects are identifiable** at any stage. The
matrix below covers the common cases.

| Data collected in | Data analyzed at | IRBs typically needed |
|---|---|---|
| India | Yale + IFMR | Yale HSC + IFMR HSC |
| Nepal | Yale + Governance Lab | Yale HSC + NHRC |
| Multiple countries | Yale + local hubs | Yale HSC + each local IRB |
| US (admin data only) | Yale | Yale HSC (often exempt) |

::: {.pitfalls}
"De-identified" data is not automatically exempt from IRB review when the
research team has the key. If you (or anyone at IE) can re-identify a record,
it's still human subjects research at most IRBs.
:::

## Submission paths by hub

::: {.panel-tabset}
## YIE (Yale HSC)

Yale uses the [IRES system](https://research.yale.edu/) for HSC submissions.
Most IE studies fit one of three categories:

- **Exempt** — secondary analysis of de-identified data, certain minimal-risk
  surveys. Faster review (1–3 weeks typical).
- **Expedited** — minimal-risk human subjects research. 3–6 weeks.
- **Full board** — anything involving vulnerable populations, sensitive
  topics, or above-minimal risk. 6–10 weeks.

See [Components of an IRB Submission — Exempt](#) and
[Components of an IRB Submission — Expedited/Full](#) for the IE templates.

## IEIC (IFMR HSC)

IFMR's HSC has its own definitions and submission process. Key references:

- [IFMR HSC Definitions](#) — terminology mapping between IFMR and Yale
- [IFMR IRB Guidelines](#) — submission template and timeline

Submissions are coordinated by the IEIC research operations team.

## IEN (NHRC)

Studies in Nepal generally require Nepal Health Research Council (NHRC)
approval in addition to Yale HSC. NHRC review timelines are highly variable
(8–16 weeks); plan accordingly.
:::

## Getting added to an existing IRB {#getting-added}

If you're a new RA or RM joining an active project:

1. Complete CITI training appropriate to your hub (see [CITI training](#citi-training) below).
2. Send your CITI completion certificate to your project's RM or PI.
3. They will submit a personnel modification to the relevant IRB(s).
4. Do not access identifiable data until you receive written confirmation that
   you've been added.

## CITI training {#citi-training}

All IE staff with access to identifiable human subjects data must complete
[CITI Program](https://about.citiprogram.org/) human subjects training. The
required modules differ by hub and study type:

- **Yale-affiliated staff** — Yale's "Social and Behavioral Research" basic
  course is the default. Refresher every three years.
- **IEIC staff** — IFMR's specified CITI track.
- **IEN staff** — NHRC requirements vary by study.

Send your completion certificate to your project's RM and keep a copy in
your personal records folder.

## Modifications

Any change to study procedures, instruments, recruitment, or personnel must
be submitted as a modification to all relevant IRBs **before** the change
takes effect. Common modifications:

- Adding or removing personnel
- Changing or adding survey questions
- Expanding the sample frame
- Adding a new data source

See [Modifying an IRB-Approved Study](#) for the IE template.

::: {.pitfalls}
Adding survey questions mid-fielding is the single most common modification —
and the single most common source of post-hoc IRB headaches. If a question
is even plausibly going to be added, include it in the original submission.
:::

## Templates

All IRB submission templates live in
[the IE Dropbox]({{< meta var.dropbox-url >}}) under `IRB Templates/`.
Specifically:

- `IE_IRB_Yale_Exempt_Template.docx`
- `IE_IRB_Yale_Expedited_Template.docx`
- `IE_IRB_IFMR_Template.docx`
- `IE_IRB_NHRC_Template.docx`
- `IE_IRB_Modification_Template.docx`

::: {.who-to-ask}
- **YIE:** the YIE Research Operations lead.
- **IEIC:** your project's RM (escalate to the IEIC Research Operations lead
  for non-routine submissions).
- **IEN:** the IEN Research Operations lead.
:::
